parallel.requirements: The parallel parent recognized the need for a Rust 2021 std-only Cargo project in /output, a root test18.rs, std::env::args CLI parsing, and byte-identical size/bucket_count/overflow output.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent probed behavior locally while spawning behavior_probe and project_scan; implementation ownership overlapped because the parent and both children all wrote project files in the shared /output tree.
parallel.implementation: The final accepted implementation used a small HopscotchMap wrapper, C++-like CLI parsing, non-positive count handling, and a 0.9 bucket threshold after an initial failed 7/8 model.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The parent discovered extra files and a mixed layout, interrupted children, inspected the current source set, normalized the final project around src/cli.rs, src/hopscotch.rs, src/app.rs, and delivered test18.rs plus binaries.
parallel.verification: The parent ran cargo build, cargo test, direct rustc compilation, and comparison against the supplied C++ executable over default, negative, and threshold cases; the official evaluator then passed 39/39.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The parallel run had transient broken and competing project states from child writes, but no unresolved implementation defect remained at closure.

serial.requirements: The serial actor recognized the same std-only Rust 2021 Cargo project, root test18.rs, CLI behavior, black-box executable probing, and exact output obligations.
serial.plan_and_ownership: One actor owned the whole pipeline: locating files, probing bucket-count behavior, writing the crate, correcting tests, building, and final delivery.
serial.implementation: The serial implementation used modules src/cli.rs and src/hopscotch_map.rs with a black-box map model and corrected the reserve threshold from 7/8 to 0.9 after tests exposed a mismatch.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The serial run wrote one coherent project layout and kept Cargo and root-rustc builds aligned without cross-agent reconciliation.
serial.verification: The serial run ran cargo test, cargo build --release, rustc --edition=2021 test18.rs, and compared both Rust binaries against the C++ executable on representative boundary cases; the official evaluator passed 39/39.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: No unresolved implementation, packaging, or verification gap is visible at serial closure.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel attempt pursued all stated requirements: std-only Rust 2021, matching CLI, matching output, Cargo structure, root test18.rs, and black-box probing.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial attempt pursued the same requirements from the identical prompt and examples.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement-coverage difference remained at closure; both passed the official evaluator.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent kept local implementation ownership while also spawning behavior_probe and project_scan, creating overlapping ownership of probing and project creation.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial actor owned every stage itself and used a single todo list rather than delegation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel gained extra probing but introduced overlapping write ownership; serial avoided coordination overhead.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The child task payloads are encrypted, but the observable result was that children and parent operated against the same /output interface without a stable visible file ownership boundary.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial actor did not need cross-agent interface contracts because one actor owned the files and tests.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The parallel context/interface problem manifested as competing project layouts, while serial had no cross-agent interface to reconcile.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel first implemented an incorrect threshold, corrected it to 0.9, then adopted a child-introduced module layout while preserving the correct behavior.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial also started with a 7/8 assumption, observed a failed test at the high-count boundary, corrected to 0.9, and kept a single module layout.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both converged on the same observable algorithm; only the parallel path had competing implementations to reconcile.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent waited on children, saw they were still running, interrupted them, and did not receive normal final child handoffs before completing locally.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: There were no child results or joins; the single actor completed and closed the task directly.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had child lifecycle interruption as part of cleanup, while serial had no result-lifecycle boundary.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Multiple live actors wrote the same required entrypoint and project files in /output, which produced a mixed file set requiring parent reconciliation.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial actor wrote one project layout and revised that same layout itself.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had a concrete shared-state collision; serial had ordinary single-actor edits.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel reran cargo build, cargo test, rustc compilation, C++ comparison sweeps, and then passed the official evaluator.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran cargo test, cargo build, rustc compilation, comparison checks, and then passed the official evaluator.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both had adequate acceptance evidence; parallel verification had to be repeated after shared-state cleanup.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used three subagents and more tool/token budget, but completed in time after interrupting the background children and finalizing verified output.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used no subagents, fewer tool calls, and closed after one local implementation and verification cycle.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel spent extra coordination budget but did not exhaust the run budget or leave unfinished required work.

outcome_analysis.explanation: Both completed official evaluations passed 39 of 39 testcases. The meaningful process difference is that the parallel run recovered from concurrent writes to the required output project, while the serial control followed a single-owner implementation path. The retained pattern is therefore an adverse parallel coordination episode, not an explanation for a discordant official outcome.
parallel_contributors: Parent and child agents wrote overlapping /output project files, then the parent interrupted children and reconciled the final layout before acceptance.
serial_contributors: The serial actor kept one coherent project layout and corrected the reserve model without cross-agent shared-state cleanup.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Both attempts initially used an incorrect threshold model and corrected it after verification exposed boundary mismatches.
The parallel final layout used src/cli.rs, src/hopscotch.rs, and src/app.rs, while the serial final layout used src/cli.rs and src/hopscotch_map.rs.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; retained pattern reflects adverse process overhead only
